## Environment set up
Notes: This analysis uses the following R packages:

- **dplyr** for data manipulation
- **ggplot2** for data visualization 

```{r loading_packages}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

```


## Introduction

This report analyzes temperature patterns and rainfall distribution across major Nigerian cities using R-based data manipulation and visualization techniques.


### Data Creation

```{r creating data.frame, message= FALSE, warning= FALSE}
weather <- data.frame(
  city = rep(c("Lagos", "Abuja", "Port Harcourt", "Kano"), each = 5),
  day = rep(1:5, times = 4),
  temperature = c(32, 34, 33, 35, 36, 
                  30, 31, 32, 33, 34,
                  31, 32, 33, 34, 35,
                  35, 36, 37, 38, 39),
  rainfall = c(10, 5, 8, 2, 0,
               2, 0, 1, 0, 0, 
               12, 10, 8, 6, 4,
               0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
) 

weather
```


### Data Cleaning

```{r}
weather_clean <- weather %>%
  mutate(temp_status = case_when(
       temperature >= 37 ~ "Very Hot",
       temperature >= 33 ~ "Hot",
       TRUE ~ "Normal"))

weather_clean
```


### Data Reshaping

```{r}
weather_long <- weather_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(temperature, rainfall),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value"
  )

weather_long
```


### Data Analysis

```{r}
avg_temp_per_city <- weather_clean %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(avg_temp = mean(temperature), .groups = "drop")

total_rainfall_per_city <- weather_clean %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(total_rainfall = sum(rainfall), .groups = "drop")

max_temp_per_city <- weather_clean %>%
  group_by(city) %>%
  summarise(max_temp = max(temperature), .groups = "drop")
summary_table <- avg_temp_per_city %>%
  left_join(max_temp_per_city, by = "city") %>%
  left_join(total_rainfall_per_city, by = "city")
summary_table

```


### Visualization

#### Bar Chart

```{r}
ggplot(data = summary_table, aes(x = city, y = avg_temp, fill = city)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Temperature by City",
    x = "City",
    y = "Temperature"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```


#### Line Chart

```{r}
ggplot(data = weather_clean, aes(x = day, y = temperature, color = city, group = city)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Temperature Trend by City",
    x = "Day",
    y = "Temperature"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ city) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```


#### Rainfall Chart

```{r}
ggplot(data = summary_table, aes(x = city, y = total_rainfall, fill = city)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Rainfall Per City",
    x = "City",
    y = "Rainfall"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```


## Key Insights

- Kano recorded the highest temperatures overall
- Lagos showed moderate but consistent temperature levels
- Port Harcourt had the highest rainfall levels
- Abuja had the lowest rainfall across the period
